getting-around: I usually walk to school. On wet days I take the bus. Last Saturday my uncle drove me to the coast. We took a ferry to the island. We used a bicycle on the island because it was easy to park.
before-the-trip: When I got to the station, my friends had already bought the tickets. They had been waiting for twenty minutes, but the train had not arrived. We waited another five minutes and then got on.
by-tomorrow: I start packing at four. By six, I will have packed both bags. My brother starts driving at seven in the morning. By nine, he will have been driving for two hours. We hope to reach the beach by ten.
bus-rules: Here’s a quick note for tomorrow’s trip. Bring a bus ticket and show it when you get on. You can bring a snack, but lunch is included. We meet at the main gate at a quarter past seven, and the coach leaves at half past.
road-trip: On Saturday morning we’re going to drive to the mountains. In the afternoon we’re going to walk around the lake. We’re not going to camp because it may rain. We booked a small hotel in the village.
at-the-hotel: Hello, this is River Hotel. Your room is ready from two in the afternoon. If you arrive earlier, you can leave your bag with us. Breakfast is included, but parking costs six dollars a day. Please tell us if you need two beds.
going-out: Have you ever been to an outdoor movie? I went to one with Ana last June. The movie was funny, but the seats were uncomfortable. If you go, take a cushion. I’ve never seen a live band in that park, but they have concerts there too.
a-famous-voice: Lina started singing at school when she was twelve. She recorded her first song in 2021. Since then she has worked with three local bands. She has never sung in another country, but she is going to travel to Peru next month.
would-you-like: Hi Joel. Would you like to go to the film festival on Friday? My sister can drop us off at six. Hey, thanks for asking. I can’t make Friday because I have practice, but I’m free on Saturday. Is there another showing then?
tense-check: I usually study in the library. This week it’s closed, so I’ve been studying at home. Yesterday, while I was reading, my friend called. I had already finished my notes. Tomorrow at this time, I’ll be studying with her.
trip-and-show: We’re taking the train on Saturday. You don’t have to print the ticket, but keep it on your phone. We’ll leave our bags at the hotel first. The show starts at eight. Have you ever seen this group? I saw them last summer and they were great.
listen-for-details: Hi Eva. The concert is still at seven, but our meeting place has changed. Don’t wait outside the cinema. Meet me at the café next door at quarter to seven. I’ve already bought both tickets. Bring a jacket because we’re walking back after the concert.
present-your-idea: Our group is going to show three ways to get to school. First, Leo will introduce the topic. Maya will explain why walking is useful. I’ll talk about the bus and give one disadvantage. At the end we’ll ask the class which way they would choose and why.
